Rashi on Pesachim 77b:10:1.hebrew: עומר ושתי הלחם דליכא עולין - לבד הקומץ, שהוא במנחה כזריקת דם בזבחים, אבל בשיריים ליכא הקטרה. וכיון דבעי ר' יהושע תרתי, צריך להיות קומץ ושיריים קיימין, והכא שיריים ליכא. ושתי הלחם, דכוליה אכילות, אפילו חדא נמי ליכא. בשלמא לר"א, דאית ליה הציץ מרצה על אכילות, כולהו כמאן דלא איטמו נינהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:10:1.english: The omer and the two loaves, of which there are no [parts that] go up [onto the altar] - [That is,] aside from the handful, which in a meal-offering is like the sprinkling of the blood in animal offerings; however, in the remainder there is no burning [on the altar]. And since Rabbi Yehoshua requires two [parts], both the handful and the remainder must be intact, and here there is no [valid] remainder. And [as for] the two loaves, which are entirely for eating, there is not even one [part]. It is understandable according to Rabbi Eliezer, who holds that the frontplate (tzitz) propitiates for eating — all of them are as though they did not become impure.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:10:2.hebrew: כי אמר ר' יהושע - דבעינן תרתי:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:10:2.english: When Rabbi Yehoshua said - that we require two.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:11:1.english: Its remainder became ritually impure - [The remainder] of a meal-offering, after its handful was removed and its handful had not yet been burned [on the altar].

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:11:2.hebrew: כמדת ר' אליעזר - שהיה אומר בזבחים (ד' קד.) "דם אף על פי שאין בשר", כשירה להקטיר קומצה ונפטרו הבעלים:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:11:2.english: According to the principle of Rabbi Eliezer - Who would say in Zevachim (104a), "[The] blood [is valid] even though there is no meat" — [therefore, the meal-offering] is valid to burn its handful [on the altar], and the owners have fulfilled [their obligation].

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:12:1.english: And who is this tanna, etc. - Where do we find a tanna who says so?

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:13:1.hebrew: מילתיה <abbr title="דרבי">דר'</abbr> יוסי מיפרשא לקמן בשמעתין:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:13:1.english: Rabbi Yosei's statement is explained later in our sugya.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:15:1.hebrew: אלא קסבר רבי יהושע הציץ מרצה על אכילות - ומיתוקמא מתני' אליביה, דהא איכא תרתי. וגבי שתי הלחם נמי, כיון דציץ מרצה על אכילות, הוה ליה כמעיקרא ומתירין במקדש:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:15:1.english: Rather, Rabbi Yehoshua holds [that] the frontplate appeases for [portions that are] eaten - And the Mishnah is established in accordance with his [view], since there are both [the blood and the meat]. And with regard to the Two Loaves as well, since the frontplate appeases for [portions that are] eaten, it is [considered] as [it was] originally, and they permit [the new grain] in the Temple.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:16:1.hebrew: אי הכי נטמאו שיריה - כיון דנטמאו לר' יהושע, אמאי פסולין? ומשני: כי קתני פסולה, אאבדו שיריה ונשרפו שיריה:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:16:1.english: If so, [when] its remnants became ritually impure - Since they became ritually impure, according to Rabbi Yehoshua, why are they disqualified? And [the Gemara] answers: When it teaches "disqualified," [it is] regarding [a case where] its remnants were lost or its remnants were burned.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:17:1.english: Rather, [where] its remainder became impure - Since Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree regarding it, [according to whom is the Mishnah teaching it?]

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:17:2.hebrew: למאן קתני לה לר' אליעזר וכו' - להודיע לנו דברי מי שנאה? להודיענו בה דברי רבי אליעזר, דלמדתו כשירה — בתמיה! פשיטא, השתא י"ל כו'. אלא פשיטא, על כרחיך ר' יהושע פליג עלה, ולאשמעינן דרבי יהושע פסיל בה תניא, ורבותא אשמעינן, דאף על גב דאיתא בעינא — פסול:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:17:2.english: According to whom does it teach it? According to Rabbi Eliezer, etc. - To inform us whose words it taught? [Is it] to inform us thereby the words of Rabbi Eliezer, that [according to] his teaching it is valid?! [This is asked] in astonishment: It is obvious! Now [that] one can say, etc. Rather, it is obvious [that] perforce Rabbi Yehoshua disagrees with it, and it was taught to inform us that Rabbi Yehoshua disqualifies it; and it teaches us a novel point, that even though it is intact, it is disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:18:1.hebrew: ולא על העולין - דהיינו חלב, דאי מרצי אחד מינייהו, אמאי פסול:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:18:1.english: Nor for [the parts] that go up - That is, the fat; for if [the frontplate] effected acceptance for one of them, why would it be invalid?

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:19:1.hebrew: אלא לא קשיא - מתני' ודרבי יהושע: מתני' דיעבד, ודר' יהושע לכתחלה. תרתי בעי, ואי אייתוה מתכשר דיעבד:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:19:1.english: Rather, it is not difficult - [between] the Mishnah and [the statement of] Rabbi Yehoshua: the Mishnah [refers to] after the fact, and [the statement of] Rabbi Yehoshua [refers to] ab initio — he requires both [meat and blood], and if they brought it [the blood alone], it is valid after the fact.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:1:1.hebrew: והני תרי קראי - לר' יהושע, למה לי:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:1:1.english: And these two verses - According to Rabbi Yehoshua, why do I [need them]?

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:1:2.english: And one [is referring] to a peace-offering - [The word] "your sacrifices" [refers to] peace-offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:1:3.english: As [it is] totally consumed - Therefore, it is important and we are stringent with it.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:20:1.english: It was disqualified - By a tevul yom [one who immersed during the day].

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:21:1.english: One [reason] is that "disqualified" indicates after the fact, etc. - This is an objection.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:5:1.hebrew: אם כן - דכולי אתא למימר דדם מתיר בשר באכילה, ולאו למימר דם אע"פ שאין בשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:5:1.english: If so - that the entire [verse] comes to say that blood permits meat to be eaten, and not to say [that] blood [is sprinkled] even though there is no meat.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:5:2.hebrew: לכתוב ובשר זבחיך תאכל והדר והדם ישפך - והוי משמע נמי והדם ישפך תחלה קודם לאכילה, דהא לא כתיב והדם תשפוך. מאי שנא דאקדמיה לדם זבחיך ישפך ברישא:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:5:2.english: [Scripture] should have written: "and the flesh of your offerings you shall eat," and then "and the blood shall be poured out" - and it would also imply [that] "the blood shall be poured out" first, before eating, since it is not written "and the blood you shall pour out." What is different that [Scripture] placed "the blood of your offerings shall be poured out" first?

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:5:3.hebrew: ש"מ - למדרש ״ודם זבחיך ישפך״ מכ"מ:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:5:3.english: Learn from it - [It comes] to expound “and the blood of your offerings shall be poured out” [as applying] in any case [even without meat].

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:6:1.hebrew: אימורים דכי ליתנהו לא מעכבי - וכגון נטמאו או אבדו, לא מעכבי אכילת בשר, כדאמרן בתמיד נשחט (לעיל פסחים דף נט:):
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:6:1.english: Sacrificial portions, which when they are not present do not preclude - And for example, [if] they became ritually impure or were lost, they do not preclude the eating of [the] meat, as we stated in [the chapter] Tamid Nishchat (above, Pesachim 59b).

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:6:2.hebrew: כי איתנהו מעכבי - אכילת בשר, כדאמרן התם:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:6:2.english: When they are present, they preclude - [the] eating of [the] meat, as we said there.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:6:3.hebrew: דם דכי ליתיה מעכב - דהא תרווייהו מודו: אם אין דם אין בשר, דמתחלת הקדשן הן נאסרין, וכפרה אינה באה אלא בדם, וכהנים משולחן גבוה קא זכו. וכיון דכפרה ליתיה, איסורא להיכא אזל:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:6:3.english: Blood, which precludes [acceptance] when it is not present - For both of them agree [that] if there is no blood, there is no meat; for from the beginning of their consecration they are forbidden, and atonement comes only through the blood, and the priests acquire [their portion] from the table of the Most High. And since there is no atonement, where did the prohibition go?

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:7:1.hebrew: לימא דלא כר' יהושע - אמילתיה קא מהדר, דאמרן לעיל מתני' דלא כר' יהושע:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:7:1.english: Shall we say [that it is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua - [The Gemara] is returning to its [earlier] statement, for we said above [that] the Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:8:1.english: We require two [things] - Blood and meat.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:8:2.hebrew: וציץ אאכילות לא מרצי - והשתא בשר ליכא, אלא דם לחודיה דמרצי ציץ עלה, ה"נ דלא אתו בטומאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:8:2.english: And the frontplate does not effect acceptance for [things] eaten - And now there is no [valid] meat, only blood alone upon which the frontplate effects acceptance; so too, they cannot be brought in [a state of] ritual impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 77b:9:1.hebrew: הציץ מרצה על העולין - על טומאת הנקטרין על האשים, דהיינו אימורין, מודי רבי יהושע דאי איכא כזית חלב לאכילת מזבח, זורק את הדם, כדאמר לקמן בברייתא בפירקין (פסחים ד' עט.): רבי יהושע אומר, כל הזבחים שבתורה שנשתייר מהן כזית בשר או כזית חלב, זורק הדם:
Rashi on Pesachim 77b:9:1.english: The frontplate appeases for that which goes up - For the impurity of those [parts] that are burned upon the fires, that is, the sacrificial portions [emurin], Rabbi Yehoshua agrees that if there is an olive-bulk of fat for the consumption of the altar, he sprinkles the blood, as it states later in a baraita in our chapter (Pesachim 79a): "Rabbi Yehoshua says: [For] all sacrifices in the Torah from which an olive-bulk of flesh or an olive-bulk of fat remained, he sprinkles the blood."

Tosafot on Pesachim 77b:10:1.hebrew: עומר ושתי הלחם דליכא עולין מאי איכא למימר - וא"ת: ובשתי הלחם מה שייך באין בטומאה? ויש לומר: משום תנופה דאית בהו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77b:10:1.english: The omer and the two loaves, of which there are no [parts that] go up [onto the altar], what is there to say? - And if you will ask: Regarding the two loaves, how does [the rule that] they are brought in ritual impurity apply? One can say: because of the waving that is [performed] with them:

Tosafot on Pesachim 77b:15:1.hebrew: קסבר ר' יהושע הציץ מרצה על העולין - וא"ת: לענין מה מפיק קרא בעולה "אם אין בשר אין דם", הלא הציץ מרצה? ויש לומר: לענין אבוד ושרוף, דלא מרצה ציץ:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77b:15:1.english: Rabbi Yehoshua holds [that] the frontplate appeases for [the impurity of] the limbs that go up [onto the altar] - And if you will say: Regarding what [case] does the verse derive concerning a burnt offering [that] "if there is no flesh, there is no blood" — does the frontplate not appease [for impurity]? And one can say: Regarding [flesh that is] lost or burned, where the frontplate does not appease.

Tosafot on Pesachim 77b:19:1.hebrew: אלא פשיטא ר' יהושע קתני לה - תימה לרשב"א: אמאי לא משני כדלעיל — כמדת ר' יהושע דבעי תרתי, ולא כמדת ר' יהושע, דאיהו ס"ל הציץ מרצה על אכילות, ואנן סבירא לן דלא מרצה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77b:19:1.english: "Rather, it is obvious [that] Rabbi Yehoshua taught it" - It is astonishing to Rashba: Why does [the Gemara] not answer as above — [that it is] like the view of Rabbi Yehoshua, who requires two, and not like the view of Rabbi Yehoshua, for he holds [that] the frontplate effects acceptance for edible portions, whereas we hold that it does not effect acceptance?

Tosafot on Pesachim 77b:19:2.hebrew: כי אמר ר' יהושע בזבחים, במנחות לא אמר - השתא משתי הלחם לא תירץ כלום, ובלאו הכי פריך שפיר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77b:19:2.english: When Rabbi Yehoshua said [it, he said it] regarding animal offerings; regarding meal offerings, he did not say [it] - Now, regarding the Two Loaves, he did not answer anything, and even without this, [the Gemara] asks well:

Tosafot on Pesachim 77b:3:1.hebrew: שאין בשר ניתר באכילה עד שיזרק הדם - תימה: אימא דוקא שלמים דאית ביה תרי אכילות, אבל עולה מנלן? דאימא: כי היכי דלית בה מעילה אחר שנזרק הדם, כדתנן במעילה בפרק חטאת העוף (מעילה דף ט.), לית בה נמי מעילה קודם זריקה, דהאי קרא בשלמים כתיב! וי"ל דר"א לא חשיב הך חומרא. ורשב"א מתרץ דר"א יליף עולה מקל וחומר דר' יהושע, ובשלמים טרח וכתב לה קרא, כדאמר בסמוך:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77b:3:1.english: "That the meat is not permitted to be eaten until the blood is sprinkled" - This is surprising: one could say [that this applies] specifically to a peace-offering, which has two [forms of] consumption, but from where do we [derive this] for a burnt-offering? For I could say that just as there is no me'ilah [misappropriation of consecrated property] in it after the blood has been sprinkled, as we learned in Me'ilah in the chapter Chatat HaOf (Me'ilah 9a), there is also no me'ilah in it prior to the sprinkling [of the blood], since this verse is written regarding a peace-offering! And one can answer that Rabbi Eliezer does not consider this a stringency. And Rashba answers that Rabbi Eliezer derives [the law for] a burnt-offering from Rabbi Yehoshua's a fortiori inference, and regarding a peace-offering, [Scripture] took the trouble to write a verse for it, as it says shortly below.
